doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Back to Washington, Charlie Byrd trio and Woody Herman tour of 1959
summary: He left Dinah for family life in 1956, hooked up with Charlie Byrd at Washington clubs, and toured England and Saudi Arabia with Woody Herman in 1959.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And then when you went back to Washington you got hooked up with Charlie Byrd.

Yeah. When I left Dinah, because my wife and I had a son and I said well I’ve got to try domesticated life. And so I went to Washington in October of ‘56 and I started working at a club that had just opened up in January and they had a house trio and they were bringing in names on the weekends. They brought in, the first one was I think it was Lucky Thompson, and then Art Farmer, and Donald Byrd, Gene Ammons, you know they’d bring them in for maybe one or two weekends. And they went down the list of all these different people. And I stayed there for six months and a guy offered me more money and a better job with better conditions up on Connecticut Avenue and I went up there, and that’s how we hooked up with Charlie. And we worked at this club for about three months and he just started doing little trio things in between, it was like © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

intermission. And the deal went down with whoever was in charge at that club, so they were looking at another club and he said, “well look I have a little restaurant up on 18th and Columbia Road, why don’t you work with the trio up there and you can get back together for that” pending that this big club was going to open. And the deal fell through, and by that time we were starting to build up something going up there, so then we just stayed there. And then it just kept on escalating and getting better and better. And we went to Europe with Woody Herman in ‘59, and that was, he took over seven pieces and added nine British musicians, and that was the first, they called the first Anglo Saxon band to tour the states. There was Jimmy Campbell on drums, Vince Guaraldi on piano, Bill Harris on trombone, and Nat Adderley and Charlie Byrd and myself. And we picked up nine British musicians and we rehearsed for two days and we went out and toured England for three weeks. We never got back to London for three weeks. And we never saw the sun for three weeks. Never saw the sun until the day we got back into London and the sun came out, and there was people sitting in Hyde Park with their faces just looking at the sun, because they hadn’t seen the sun. And then two days later with the small group we went to Saudi Arabia for the Aramco people. That’s all we saw for eight days, pure sun, no clouds, pure sun.
